## Findings
- [ ] **[WARN][Coverage] Real update-check/install adapter implementations untested**
  - **Status quo:** `AppUpdateChecker.swift` (59.5%) and `UpdateInstaller.swift` (53.1%) — the pure logic (`performInstall`) is 95.6% covered via injected fakes, but every real adapter (`DefaultUpdateFileSystem`, `DefaultUpdateProcessRunner`, `URLSessionAssetDownloader`, `ProcessAppRelauncher`, `UserDefaultsSkippedVersionStore`, plus the `@MainActor` `install`/`currentTeamIdentifier` wrappers) is 0% covered.
  - **Likely cause:** Tests deliberately avoid touching real disk/network/process via DI, but never separately verify the thin adapters against the real APIs they wrap.
  - **Proposed solution:** See `.github/coverage/2026-07-09T15-57-37Z.md` for the specific adapter-level test plan (temp files, temp `UserDefaults` suite, a harmless real subprocess).
  - **Handoff:** `/02-gh-plan --from-coverage .github/coverage/2026-07-09T15-57-37Z.md` → `/03-gh-go`
  - This is WARN, not BLOCK: the repo has no hard coverage gate, and the core logic that matters most (the actual verify/swap/rollback decision tree) is well covered.

- [ ] **[WARN][Assets] No release pipeline publishes a `.app` zip asset yet**
  - **Status quo:** This release ships `AppUpdateChecker`/`UpdateInstaller`, which assume a downloadable zipped `SymDesk.app` GitHub Release asset — none is currently published; `.goreleaser.yml`/`release.yml` only build the Go CLI binaries.
  - **Likely cause:** Known and already tracked — flagged on issue #70 during implementation, not new to this gate.
  - **Proposed solution:** No action needed from this gate; tracked as a follow-up issue candidate for whoever wires the updater into the actual UI.
  - **Handoff:** none required to release v0.5.0 — the shipped code is internal plumbing with no user-facing entry point yet, so its assumption being unmet does not block or regress anything live.
